turn_text: This week on Indivisible Westchester at the podcast, Congressman Elliot Engle gives us the latest on impeachment and also an update on the conflict with Iran. Congressman L.A.T. Angle joins me today. Congressman Angle, you are one of the impeachment managers. Can you tell me what the latest update with impeachment is at this point?

Well, we believe in a little while in a short time that Nancy Pelosi will be sending over the papers of impeachment to the Senate. And we hope that Mitch McConnell and the other senators will treat it with the seriousness it deserves. And hopefully there will be a trial with witnesses. because whoever heard of a trial without witnesses, and whatever happens happens, but the American people deserve to have a trial.
So tell me, Congressman, what are you doing to try and ensure that there are witnesses, or at least to do your part to see that Moscow Mitch does his part?

Well, first of all, if he can be embarrassed at all, I'm not really sure that he can be, but we really want to let the public know that this is so important and it's not something that's going to be swept under the rug. This is important. This is the way our government works. It can't be where it's inconvenient for Mitch McConnell or for the president or anybody else and therefore they just disregard what Congress did. They have to take it seriously and we have to play it out to the fullest way that it really makes sense and I'm hoping that they take it seriously. If they don't then we'll be quick to point it out because I'm not and I know others are not going to let this be swept under the rug.

turn_text: That was going to be almost one of my questions. What is your greatest concern at this point now when it comes to the impeachment process?

Well, my greatest concern first of all is that on the Republican side, the senators don't seem to have their own mind. They're not voting their own mind. They're doing what they're told, what the president wants, what the leadership wants. That's not what really supposed to happen on a serious issue. If you don't want to convict the president, then vote against convicting him, but have a fair and free trial. Don't make fun of it by ignoring it or by not adhering to what is supposed to be done. So that's my concern because once you do that, it's a slippery slope. You know, we just had a big battle in Congress this week. I led the charge on the House floor to tell the president that he doesn't declare a war, Congress declares a war, and he cannot carry on a war with his own declaration. Congress declares a war. The war powers are very important. So we're looking at the war powers and insisting that they be adhered to.

So we had a so-called classified briefing, which was very frustrating because We all walked out of their scratching our heads. And that was supposed to be telling us what happened. There was no mention made of embassies, different embassy bombings. And now suddenly this is the new thing that the administration and the president keeps talking about, of imminent threat that were going to bomb embassies. If that was the case, why weren't we told about it when we had our briefing, our classified briefing. So it's very hard, you know, you want to believe what they say, but you just don't know what you can because their policies, their attitudes, seems to be, tell the Congress the smallest amount of material that you can get away with and try to treat Congress as an irrelevancy. Again, that's not what the founding fathers had in mind. We have the three branches of government, checks and balances, the executive branch, the legislative branch, the judicial branch that's been tested for years and years. And now they want to just essentially rule by fiat. We can't allow that. And I think there are lots of things. that are going to come out. John Bolton has said that he would testify if he's subpoenaed. He should be subpoenaed. What are they afraid of? Let the truth be known. If they want to refute anything, he says they can do that.
